chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, and Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Muthanna Al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked: A woman left behind her mother, and her full siblings (from father and mother), and her paternal siblings (from father only), and her maternal siblings (from mother only). He said: 'For her paternal siblings (from father and mother) are two-thirds, and for her mother is one-sixth, and for her maternal siblings is one-sixth.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance shares for full, paternal, and maternal siblings when the mother is also alive?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific distribution of inheritance among full, paternal, and maternal siblings alongside the mother, a scenario often discussed in the context of the 'Kalalah' or complex family structures in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that full siblings collectively receive two-thirds, while the mother and maternal siblings each receive one-sixth, reflecting the application of the Quranic shares (Fara'id) within the framework of the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation. This ruling is significant for understanding how Shia scholars reconcile these specific fractional shares when multiple categories of heirs coexist.
